title: Audio system: material×event bank, scale-aware acoustics, spatialized mix (AUTH #022)
summary: Build the v1 audio system per SPEC §3.6 and Movement Bible §9: a material × event sound bank covering every verb and tool, contact-frame-locked to the animation, layered + round-robin + impact-scaled; 3D spatialization with an ambience bed and category mix buses (movement/world/tools/UI/music) with sidechain ducking; scale-aware pitch/gain; scale-aware acoustic reverb computed from the reconstructed room (volume + material absorption); restrained adaptive music (ambient bed + sparse stings + the shrink-transition theme). CC0/royalty-free/self-recorded sourcing only. Brain-B half (the bank data + the scale-aware acoustics reference + coverage/validation) is built; the Unity audio engine + CC0 clips are gj-gameplay.
deliverables: unity (audio engine, SurfaceMaterial event bank, reverb-from-scenegraph, mix buses) [gj-gameplay]
services/audio + data/audio (bank data + scale-aware acoustics + AudioMixer/bus config + tests) [claude-builder, done]

acceptance_tests.test: The material × event bank covers all v1 verbs and tools (incl. grapple pin/twine, pole-vault, wall-run, dive-roll), fires on animation contact frames, and is round-robin + impact-scaled so a 2-minute run has no machine-gun repetition.
acceptance_tests.evidence: test scene + audio log; bank coverage of the frozen verb enum proven by services/audio/tests/test_bank.py

acceptance_tests.test: Scale-aware acoustic reverb is computed from the scene graph (room volume + material absorption) and audibly differs between a small dead room and a large live one.
acceptance_tests.evidence: A/B capture of two corpus rooms; reference proven by services/audio/tests/test_acoustics.py (Sabine; big-live > small-dead)

acceptance_tests.test: Pitch, gain, and reverb size scale with the environment multiplier (Lego clicks tiny, floor booms big); category mix buses + ducking keep critical cues (summit/vista/flag) audible; audio is 3D-spatialized.
acceptance_tests.evidence: test scene; scale pitch/gain reference proven by services/audio/tests/test_acoustics.py

acceptance_tests.test: All audio is CC0/royalty-free/self-recorded with provenance recorded; the bank fits the mobile audio memory + polyphony budget.
It sounds real and alive on the Owner's iPhone.

history.event: created by the Coordinator as an AUTH #022 follow-up (audio system).

Brain-B half built. services/audio + data/audio: the scale-aware acoustics reference (acoustics.py + acoustics.json — Sabine reverb from scene_graph volume + 11-material absorption; scale pitch/gain from scale.multiplier with per-event weight so booms stay big) and the material×event sound bank (sound_bank.json + bank.py — every verb/tool/landing/reaction/UI/music event with bus/layers/round-robin/impact/weight/material, validated for coverage against the frozen traversal_graph verb enum). 15 tests prove AT-1 coverage, AT-2 big-live>small-dead reverb, and AT-3 scale pitch/gain. qa/audio-sources.md provenance scaffold (AT-4 policy). No protected path (AUTH #022 already applied to SPEC/Bible; data under data/audio, not data/schemas). Remaining: the Unity audio engine (mixer buses + ducking, 3D spatialization, contact-frame wiring) and the CC0 clips (gj-gameplay); the C# engine mirrors data/audio like movement.json.

Brain-B follow-on: the AudioMixer/bus config as data (services/audio/mixer.py + data/audio/mixer.json). Master + the five category buses (matching the sound bank), a scale-aware reverb send bus fed by the diegetic buses (ui/music stay dry), sidechain ducking (a ui cue ducks movement/world so a landing warning always reads; music stings duck action; ambience ducks under movement), per-bus voice budget + priority, mobile polyphony ceiling. validate_mixer cross-checks buses against the sound bank. 9 mixer tests (24 audio total). Remaining AT-3 'critical cues audible + 3D-spatialized' and the mixer graph wiring are the Unity engine (gj-gameplay), which mirrors data/audio/mixer.json.

Built the audio-source generation recipe (services/audio/sources.py + data/audio/source_manifest.json; 11 tests, 36 audio total). build_manifest turns the bank into a vendor-agnostic plan: one spec per event (62), material-varying events expanded over the 10 concrete scene_graph materials, each with a text prompt, clip count (= round_robin), loop/one-shot flag, duration, and the ffmpeg post-process (ffmpeg_filters: one-shots trimmed + loudness-normalised; loops left raw for a seamless boundary). validate_manifest enforces bank coverage; a drift test pins source_manifest.json to the bank. The generator is an AudioProvider port -- DryRunProvider runs the plan at $0; a real provider (ElevenLabs via FAL is the natural candidate) needs a spend/account AUTH and holds no key in-repo. Prompt shapes adapted from the MIT image-blaster project; ambience beds take their prompt from the vision-pass survey's ambient_sound. This closes the qa/audio-sources.md sourcing gap with a concrete plan -- no protected path, no new vendor/spend. The clip files themselves + any provider procurement remain gj-gameplay + AUTH-gated.

Built the ElevenLabs generation provider + batch runner (AUTH #048). services/audio/elevenlabs_provider.py implements the sources.AudioProvider port against ElevenLabs text-to-sound-effects (POST /v1/sound-generation, model eleven_text_to_sound_v2): the API key is read from ELEVENLABS_API_KEY (env/CI secret, never committed) and the HTTP call is injectable so tests run with no network/spend; each request maps to {text=prompt, duration_seconds, loop, prompt_influence, output_format}. services/audio/generate_audio.py walks the manifest, generates, saves, and applies the ffmpeg post-process; it DEFAULTS TO A DRY RUN ($0, no key) and caps real runs with --limit (the full manifest is ~1,841 calls / 422 families -> run capped + incrementally). Generated clips are git-ignored (services/audio/_generated/); provenance in qa/audio-sources.md. 9 new tests (45 audio total; mock provider, no network/spend). The Owner authorized ElevenLabs on their own account (AUTH #048); running the real batch is the Owner/Operator's step once ELEVENLABS_API_KEY is set, and the Unity audio engine + StreamingAssets wiring remain gj-gameplay.

Wired the CI run path: the Owner added ELEVENLABS_API_KEY to GitHub Actions secrets, so generation runs in a job, not from a session shell (Actions secrets are not exposed to the agent's shell). Added .github/workflows/audio-generate.yml (workflow_dispatch; inputs event/material/limit; maps ELEVENLABS_API_KEY from secrets; runs generate_audio.py --execute capped by --limit; uploads clips as a 7-day artifact, never committed) and coerced empty CI inputs to 'all' in generate_audio.main. A ~1-call smoke (event=ui-publish, limit=1) is dispatched to prove the end-to-end path before any wider, capped batch (full manifest ~1,841 calls).

Full manifest generated on the Owner's ElevenLabs account (AUTH #048, $25 cap). Root-caused two silent misfires first: GitHub workflow_dispatch swaps an empty-string input for the field's default, so a blank `event` ran only the ui-publish default (1 clip) instead of the manifest. Fix (commit 1f3ea8a, green CI, FF main): a non-empty `all` sentinel -- generate_audio._resolve_filter maps 'all'/blank -> every event/material; non-empty inputs transmit unchanged -- plus a test and workflow docs. Then dispatched event=all/material=all/limit=2000 (run 37401926240): written_files=1841/1841, failed_families=0, provider_calls=1841, ~46 min, artifact gj-audio-all (18,695,647 bytes, 7-day retention). Spend ~1,841 calls / ~70,800 credits (+ ~72 walk-chunk + 2 smoke clips from the misfires) ~= $12-17, within the $25 cap. Clips stay git-ignored; gj-gameplay pulls the artifact and wires StreamingAssets. Gives AT-4 real generated candidates; CC0/royalty-free foley may still replace any clip.

notes: Brain-B contract (services/audio + data/audio) done; the Unity engine + CC0 clips are gj-gameplay. data/audio/*.json is the source of truth the C# engine mirrors (movement.json pattern); a sync check can be added when the engine lands. Music identity = restrained adaptive stings (AUTH #022).
